MEET KNEAD

Knead is a small Abyssinian with a permanently unimpressed face. It sprawls over a ball of yellow yarn in the corner of your Windows desktop, quietly watching over a human who spends a little too long at the computer.

Most of the time, it sleeps peacefully. But when it is time for a little movement, it knows exactly how to make itself noticed.

A LITTLE MISCHIEF, FOR A REASON

Knead is not another quiet notification.

It peeks over the edge of your window, or clings on and gives the window a tiny shake.

It steals a little attention on purpose—just enough to break through your focus and lure you away from your work for a moment. Each interruption is brief, playful, and unmistakably feline.

A FEW MINUTES, THEN BACK TO WORK

Interacting with Knead opens a compact guided-movement window. It demonstrates one simple, desk-friendly movement at a time, accompanied by a short instruction and timer.

A little stretch, a little movement, and a short break becomes a moment together. Afterwards, you can return to whatever you were doing.

A LITTLE MOVEMENT, A LITTLE GROWTH

Usually, Knead is the one looking out for you. You can look after it too, with a little food in its bowl and some fresh water beside it.

The moments you spend moving and caring for it help it grow, and find their way into your shared journal. Every now and then, you can turn back a few pages and see how much time you have spent together.

COME THE WEEKEND, IT HAS PLANS OF ITS OWN

On weekends and holidays, you can plan a little journey for Knead on its hand-drawn map. While you take some time away from work, it gets to see the world beyond your desktop.

A journey usually lasts a full weekend or holiday break. It will generally send a letter on the first day, letting you know how life on the road is treating it.

When it comes home, there will be mysterious gifts tucked away in its bag. What they are can wait until you are together again.

NOT NOW? A LITTLE LATER

When the timing is not right, Knead can wait a little longer. It goes back to rest for a while before coming to find you again.

The cat may be persistent, but it still knows when to give you room. The timing of the break remains in your hands.

QUIET COMPANY, TOO

For a meeting, screen sharing, or simply a little quiet, you can temporarily hide Knead and bring it back when you are ready.

Knead is not here to manage your day. It just wants to make taking a little break easier—and feel a little more like playing with a cat.

You wake up in a room you don’t recognize. No windows. No way out. Just a door… and the unsettling feeling that someone —or something— is watching you.

In Knock Again, you must knock on the door to earn money, upgrade your abilities, and… keep knocking. It sounds simple, almost absurd. But with each passing day, the room changes. The invisible presence on the other side becomes harder to ignore.

This is not a normal clicker. It’s a psychological horror game where mechanical progress hides something dark, twisted, and uncomfortable. Monotony distorts. Logic breaks. And all you can do is keep knocking, hoping it brings you closer to the truth… or at least keeps whatever’s on the other side away.

How far are you willing to go to escape?

Koishi’s Fishing Journal is a Touhou Project fan-made desktop idle fishing game starring Koishi Komeiji. Let Koishi relax and fish in a corner of your desktop. Even while you work, study, or do other things, she will keep fishing and bring back all kinds of catches.

Relax and Fish, Decorate Your Desktop

There’s no need to watch the game all the time. Koishi keeps fishing on your desktop; check back now and then to see what she has caught today, then let her carry on at her leisure. You can also choose your favorite decorations for Koishi and decorate her little fishing corner on your desktop. Let Koishi keep you company in a look you like while you work or study, adding something fresh to your familiar desktop.

Relax and Fish with Friends or Strangers

Invite friends to your room, or find strangers to quietly idle with. Bring everyone’s Koishi together on your desktop, with up to 12 players fishing together. Chat as you fish and enjoy multiplayer bonuses, or enable shared clicks to give each other a hand with fishing. Take a break from work or study to chat now and then and see how many fish everyone has caught.

From Ordinary Fish to Mermaids

The waters are home to species of all shapes and sizes. The most common ordinary fish can be used directly as cooking ingredients, while rarer merfolk species provide precious cooking ingredients that ordinary fish cannot. Among the merfolk is an exceptionally rare, highest-tier species—mermaids.
Keep discovering new fish and merfolk, expand your species collection, and seek out those rarely seen species.

Cook Dishes and Sell Them in Your Shop

Turn the ordinary fish you catch and the precious ingredients obtained from merfolk into a variety of dishes, then put the finished dishes in your shop to sell automatically. Spend your earnings on upgrades to make fishing easier and give yourself a chance to encounter more rare fish and merfolk.
Check back now and then to see your new catches, cook dishes, and restock your shop, then let Koishi carry on fishing at her leisure.

Set up your chefs to cook automatically and earn money with ease. You can also run a stall yourself, complete orders, and earn substantial income.

Fish, cook, and collect merfolk. Enjoy a leisurely desktop fishing life with Koishi.

In 1997, Kritsana told his psychiatrist that something was in his house.

He set up cameras to record what was happening in the house. Dr. Thanapat watched the tapes, read his notes, and wrote it off as a hallucination.

Then things kept happening.

2004. The case file is on your desk. The tapes are still in the box. So are the doctor's notes. Your job is to go through all of it again and see what everyone missed.

WHERE THE TAPES WERE RECORDED

Four places from the case, all in rural Thailand:

- Kritsana's grocery store, where he lived
- The auto repair shop where his father worked
- Dr. Thanapat's clinic
- The local temple

HOW IT WORKS

Switch between cameras and look for anything that changes. Most of it is small. A jar that wasn't on the shelf a minute ago. A door that should be closed.

Some of it isn't small. Footprints show up on the floor. A bird drops dead in front of the camera. The alarm goes off in a shop with nobody in it.

When you see something, report it. Keep watching until 5:00 AM.

Make five incorrect reports in a row, or let four anomalies pile up at once, and the system fails. You'll have to start over.

THE CASE OPENS UP AS YOU PLAY

Before and after each tape, you go through the evidence: the doctor's notes, the records, what was left behind. Finish a location and the file shows you more. Find every anomaly there and you get everything it has to give.

There's one ending. How much of it makes sense depends on how much you've found.

FEATURES

- 200+ anomalies across four locations
- Around 2 hours for a first playthrough, and a lot more if you want to find everything
- Slow, quiet horror. There are a few jump scares, but mostly it's just you and the silence
- English and Thai voice acting, with subtitles in English, Simplified Chinese, Russian, Spanish, Portuguese, German, Japanese, French, Korean, Thai, and Indonesian
- Made by a team from Thailand

A breathtaking adventure.

Out now. 10% off for launch week.

"Dive into a mysterious underwater world where every breath matters and every discovery invites you deeper."
Hype Expert, Steam Curator

"A charming adventure that combines exploration, thoughtful resource management and permanent equipment upgrades."
ScreenScribe, Steam Curator

One tank of air. A whole ocean to read.
Kyle Coral is a cave-diving adventure with no countdown and no score to chase. Swim from the sunlit Shallows to a bioluminescent Abyss, find air pockets to breathe, and reach each exit before your tank runs dry.

  • Every dive is a new cave, drawn fresh
  • Five biomes, four guardians waiting in the dark
  • Pearls buy permanent gear at the Trading Post. What you buy, you keep.
  • Full controller support, a colorblind aid, and an opt-in Assist Mode

Try it free. The demo covers the first seven levels, all the way to the Giant Moray. Hit Download Demo above.

Air is the only clock

Nothing ticks on screen. Your tank is the tension: a held breath, not a stopwatch. Spot the shimmer of an air pocket, plan the next stretch, and push a little deeper.

Guardians in the dark

The Kelp Forest, the Deep Blue, the Sunken Ruins and the Abyss each end with a guardian, starting with the Giant Moray.

Gear you keep

Pry pearls from clams and spend them at the Trading Post between biomes: a knife, a harpoon, a scuba tank, a dive light. Missing gear makes a dive harder, never impossible.

A living sea

Shoals scatter as you pass, kelp sways in the current, and the light fades as you descend. Every cave is generated fresh, so no two dives look the same.

Forgiving by design

The pressure is real without being cruel.

Some caves hold more than pearls. What the deep is hiding is yours to find.

YOU ARE A LEG EMOJI

That's it. One leg.

Walking should be the one thing you are good at.

Unfortunately, walking is hard.

LEG DAY: Four Steps Through Hell is a physics platformer about learning to control one stubborn leg and dragging it through an increasingly difficult and absurd world.

MASTER THE LEG

Movement is driven by physics. Learn how the leg reacts, control its balance and use momentum to climb through platforms, slopes, water, caves and other increasingly ridiculous challenges.

FOUR STEPS THROUGH HELL

Your journey begins bright, strange and almost friendly. It does not stay that way.

Each stage introduces new environments, mechanics and ways to lose your progress as the world becomes darker, harder and more unpredictable.
You are only one leg.

How far can you go?

Britain's greatest super-weapon rides again!

A giant wheel, and a driver on each side of it.
You take the left wheel. Your partner takes the right.
That is the entire control scheme, and driving in a straight line has never been this hard.

One machine, two people

  • Charge your own wheel to move. Spin harder than your partner and you will simply turn on the spot
  • Fire your side thrusters to straighten up. Mistime it and you go straight over the cliff
  • The moment one of you stops, the Panjandrum takes off in a direction nobody chose
Whatever goes wrong out there, it is nobody's fault. Probably.

50 stages

Artillery, mines, drones, buzzsaws and pillars of fire. Nothing on the course is on your side.

Times and stars

  • Every stage is timed and rated with up to three stars
  • Track down the red traffic cones hidden along each course

Online two-player co-op only

This game cannot be played alone.
One player can only turn one wheel, which leaves the Panjandrum spinning on the spot.
You will need a Steam account, an internet connection, and one partner.

You have no fixed form. What you refine will shape what you become.

LIANYAO: The Formless One is a first-person deckbuilding roguelite inspired by Chinese folklore and strange tales of the wild.

Venture into haunted mountains, confront beasts, spirits, and corrupted creatures, and refine the souls of defeated monsters into powers of your own.

But refining a monster does more than give you another card.

The powers you choose will gradually shape what you become.

Turn Your Enemies' Powers Into Your Own

The monsters you fight are the source of your build.

Defeat different creatures, claim their souls, and refine their signature abilities into skills you can use yourself.

Different enemies open different combat directions: defensive retaliation, relentless pursuit, rapid multi-hit attacks, and stranger powers drawn from corrupted spirits and demons.

Rather than assembling a pre-made archetype, your deck grows from the creatures you encounter and the abilities you choose to take from them.

Let Your Build Shape Your Form

Your abilities determine more than how you fight — they gradually transform you.

As you continue refining different kinds of power, new supernatural forms begin to emerge, reinforcing the combat style you have built throughout the run.

You do not choose a fixed class at the beginning of an expedition.

What you eventually become depends on which creatures you encounter, which powers you refine, and how you combine them.

You do not choose a build first and search for the right cards.

Your build takes shape naturally through the act of refining monsters.

Take Shape Anew on Every Expedition

Every journey into the mountains brings a new combination of battles, events, blessings, relics, and monster souls.

Sometimes you will find the core of your build early. Other times, a newly acquired power may push you in an entirely different direction.

Adapt to what the expedition gives you, combine abilities and relics into powerful interactions, and gradually complete a combat style unique to that run.

There is no single path to follow.

What you encounter, what you refine, and what you leave behind will determine the shape of each expedition.

Face the Creatures of a Strange Eastern Wilderness

Enter battle from a first-person perspective and confront creatures inspired by Chinese folklore, mountain legends, and tales of wandering spirits.

Observe enemy intentions, balance offense and defense, and find openings through careful combinations of abilities.

Wild beasts are only the beginning.

As you travel deeper into the mountains, familiar creatures begin to change, unnatural forces spread through the wilderness, and far more dangerous beings reveal themselves.

Defeat them.

Refine them.

Then carry their power deeper into the unknown.

About Game：

Welcome to Black & White Limbo!

“Calamity is coming. The resentment of the dead will take monstrous form and sweep across the continent.”

Word of Archmage Grey’s prophecy reaches the Ring City. Five warriors versed in exorcism are sent forth. You are the Prince of Might, but your thoughts remain with the seaside town that raised you.

The typhoon has already arrived.

Your hometown has become a haunt of restless spirits. The faces you remember are nowhere to be found. The old king orders you to turn back. But if you abandon this place, who will stand for it?

Set forth, Prince. The dead of your homeland have yet to find peace…

Reclaim Your Homeland. Face the Yokai!

Venture into a pixel-art world overrun by yokai! Take command in turn-based battles and unleash spectacular animated skills. Every exorcist technique gets its moment to shine!

Make your way through storm-ravaged streets and into the creatures’ lairs. Follow the trail of lingering resentment to uncover the source of the catastrophe. Your journey will take you beyond anything the prophecy foretold.

“Those who exorcise monsters shall become monsters themselves…”

You ignored that warning when you set out.

Will you still press on?

…Mr. Hirata? Are You Still Playing?

Shuuichi Hirata only wanted to unwind with a game after work.

Then a baffling murder shatters his routine, and a game console comes under scrutiny.

Can a game kill?

An absurd suggestion. Yet the accounts contradict one another, and something about Hirata’s memories doesn’t add up.

Follow Hirata, Tachibana, and Watanabe as their perspectives unfold. Search for clues across animated scenes of the real world and a pixel world you can explore firsthand. Hear their stories, then decide whom to trust.

As for everything Hirata remembers…

Perhaps that deserves another look, too.

Character Files

Shuuichi Hirata Team Leader of Group A in the Marketing Division at Miura Electric Industries’ Kenhama Branch, and a veteran gamer. Gaming is his favorite way to unwind after work. Mention the actress Mikako, though, and you might get a few more words out of him.

Mikako A popular actress who got her start as an idol with a devoted following. Her name alone is enough to turn heads.

Watanabe Head of Market Division Three at the Kenhama Branch. Composed, pragmatic, and charismatic, Watanabe is almost obsessive about Kenhama’s development and knows Mikako personally.

Tachibana A former police inspector whose rough methods conceal a fierce sense of loyalty. Alongside the case he is pursuing, he carries a secret that weighs heavily on him.

Satou Tachibana’s protégée, a young officer who gets things done. Fond of puns. Whether they’re any good is for her audience to decide.

Shinichiro Fukui General Manager of the Kenhama Branch and Head of Market Division One. Overbearing and harsh, he has been testing his subordinates’ patience for a very long time.

??? No information available.

Adapted from “Hirata’s World,” a celebrated story arc in San Tian Liang Jue’s novel Thriller Paradise.

Send out the troops. Push the line. Break their stronghold.

LINE WARLORD is a real-time lane-defense roguelite. Rations refill as you fight, and every battle comes down to what you send out and when. Between battles you pick up relics, promote your units, and choose your path on a branching map. When a run ends, the upgrades you bought at the Forge and the Pantheon stay, so the next march starts a little stronger.

Features

  • Spend rations to summon troops and send them down the line. What you send, and when, decides the fight.
  • An Empower gauge fills as you fight and is used only for Army Empower. Your Ultimate runs on its own cooldown.
  • Three commanders: Loenhart, Merka and Crono. Each has a different Ultimate and a different way of fighting.
  • Stack relics, promote and awaken your unit types, and gamble on events. No two runs field the same army.
  • Three chapters, with buffs and debuffs on every map. Pick between battles, elites, shops, camps and events on a branching map, all the way to the boss.
  • Five Warfire levels: clear a run to unlock the next. Enemies hit harder, rewards grow.
  • Forge and Pantheon upgrades are permanent between runs. Available in 12 languages.

The game sends anonymous play statistics (no personal data) to help us balance it.

The ammunition is ready.
The front is still waiting.




LINETAIN puts you in charge of the supply lines. In this single-player logistics game, you connect depots, factories, fronts and hospitals, then assign a limited fleet to the routes. Loading, transfers and combat happen automatically.

A longer line isn't always a better route.



A planned connection becomes a working supply line.

More stops mean a longer wait for the next delivery. Shorter routes can share the work through a transfer point, but only if each has enough vehicles. Follow the queues and see where the plan is falling behind.

You can extend a line, cut it back or change an endpoint during a run. Construction takes time. Sometimes the vehicle you need is already out there, tied up on a route that takes too long.


One reserve vehicle joins R1. Two vehicles now share the route.

Who can spare a vehicle?




The wounded need to reach a hospital before their time runs out. Take a vehicle off a supply route to help them, and ammunition may start piling up elsewhere. Keep it on the supply run, and there's less help for the wounded.

Pause whenever you need to think. Check the next attack warning and adjust the network. Unpause and see whether the next delivery reaches the front in time.

Seven operations in Early Access




Learn the ropes in Introduction, hold out in Survival, then take on Tokyo, Berlin, Rio, London and Cairo. Meet each operation's objective to open the next. The city maps are fictional operations inspired by real places, not historical battles.

Later operations appear on the selection map as previews, but are not playable yet. Their release dates have not been announced.

Save a run when you need a break and pick it up later. Available in English and Japanese for Windows, with keyboard and mouse controls. Play offline, or connect to Steam for achievements and leaderboards.

The free demo includes Introduction, Survival and Tokyo.

YOU ARE THE OLDEST GAME THERE IS

A snake in a pit. It grows when it eats. It dies when it crosses itself.

That part has not changed in fifty years.

What you are fighting has.

A Doomscroll Gremlin. A Reply-Guy Mosquito. A CAPTCHA Crab. An Algorithm Eye. Twenty-four of them, and every one is something the internet did to you first.

They come in the hundreds. They do not get tired.

So you stop being a snake that eats, and become a snake that is built.

EVERY SEGMENT OF YOUR BODY IS A WEAPON

Kill. Level up. Spend a MOLT. A new segment grows.

FANG fires bolts. TESLA chains lightning. FROST freezes whatever gets close. EMBER burns the ground under you. MAW blasts a shotgun cone wherever that part of your body happens to be pointing.

Eleven weapons. Every one of them fires on its own.

You never aim. You steer.

Your body is not carrying the build. Your body IS the build.

THE ORDER IS THE PUZZLE

A segment only looks at its neighbors.

Put FROST next to FANG and your bolts crit anything slowed.

Put EMBER next to TESLA and every jump of the chain sets its target on fire.

Put TESLA next to LEECH and every jump heals you.

Drop a support between two weapons and it feeds both at once.

Move one segment one place and you light a reaction, kill another, and change who gets fed.

There is no inventory screen. The snake is the inventory.

FUSE, AND TRADE LENGTH FOR TEETH

Two identical neighbors fuse into one, up to Tier 3.

It is not a bigger number. It is a different shape.

Fewer segments. Heavier weapons. A shorter body that can close a tighter circle.

Grow wide, or compress hard. The snake plays differently either way.

CLOSE THE OUROBOROS

Your best attack is not aimed. It is drawn.

Steer your head around a crowd until it touches your own tail.

The loop closes. The shape is measured. Everything caught inside is executed at once.

But a tight circle packed with bodies pays better than a wide empty one.

So closing is a decision: take what you have, or go around one more time?

TWELVE FLOORS DOWN, AND SOMETHING ABOVE THE LAST ONE

The pit has twelve floors. Each one keeps a guardian, and each guardian wants a different snake than the one that beat the floor below.

Eleven climbs already failed. The Library keeps what they wrote down.

Every guardian has an eye.

You will notice that later than you should.

EL DEVORADOR DOES NOT WAIT

Ring volleys. Solar spirals. Aimed cones. A beam that sweeps. Rot falling from above. His own brood.

He fights in phases, he is reborn between them, and his Mark punishes anyone who stands still.

He is not the top of the pit. He is the first one who makes you build on purpose.

SKILL MATCH — THE MAIN EVENT

Seventeen waves, with air between them.

A mid-boss holding a chest at wave 7. A shop. And three charges of REORDER: a workshop that stops the world so that rebuilding your body is a puzzle instead of a reflex test.

This is where the machine gets designed.

ARCADE — FIVE MINUTES, NO AIR

A 5 to 7 minute run of unbroken pressure, with EL DEVORADOR arriving at 5:00 sharp.

Build fast. Adapt faster. No workshop is coming to save you.

TURN THE RISK DIAL YOURSELF

Four alchemical acts: NIGREDO. ALBEDO. CITRINITAS. RUBEDO.

Then push each one with five optional Danger rungs. Each rung is one sentence you read before you accept it, and the payout is wired to the same dial.

Some of them feed the horde. Others graft a new attack onto the boss.

Clear Danger 5 and D-HELL opens, past the top of the ladder.

LOSING PAYS

Win or lose, you keep your Scales.

You spend them in THE NEST: 29 nodes across four concentric rings, with health, damage and speed on offer in every ring, so no ring only sells you sidegrades.

One bad run buys your first node.

SOLEMN ALCHEMY, RIDICULOUS JUNK

The four acts are named after the stages of the Great Work, and the world takes that completely seriously.

Your relics are a fridge magnet, a baby tooth, a portable grill, a plunger, grandma's scarf and the leftovers of a Sunday cookout.

Neither half ever acknowledges the other.

FEATURES

  • 11 weapon segments and 2 supports, each with 3 tiers you reach by fusing

  • Neighbor-based interactions that make the ORDER of your body part of the build

  • 4 chemical reactions that only fire between adjacent segments

  • 24 enemies drawn from internet culture, and they are all trying to reach you

  • 8 playable snakes: every one starts with a different body, five change a rule of it

  • 61 items across 5 rarities, and 16 relics

  • A 29-node permanent progression tree — losing pays too

  • 4 alchemical acts, 5 optional Danger rungs, and D-HELL past the top

  • A multi-phase boss with 9 attacks in his repertoire

  • 3 Oaths: skins that change a mechanic and say so out loud

  • Leaderboards by mode, act and Danger rung

  • 22 achievements

  • Interface and subtitles in 12 languages

Something has been watching the whole climb.

The snake that eats its own tail is not a metaphor here. It is the finisher.

ONE PUZZLE. ONE DAY. THOUSANDS OF COMPETITORS.

In 2026, the Heuristic Tactics Laboratory pushes cognition to the edge with competitive protocols. LOOPY is the arena: one perfect loop, zero noise, and the rush of closing the circuit under neon.

THE DAILY RITUAL

Every UTC day, nine ranked races go live in parallel (Traditional plus eight arcade mechanics) on a 10×10 grid. You get three attempts per mode, a 3→1→GO countdown, an honest millisecond clock, and a Steam leaderboard per protocol. The server verifies the replay. Every 19th day, difficulty spikes to HARD, and the whole arena heats up.

This is not “just another grid.” It is a lab Command Deck: deep void UI, electric cyan, hot magenta focus, and every mode lighting the board with its own color signature.

OUTRUN MATRIX — COLOR WITH TEETH

LOOPY lives in the Outrun void: near-black canvas, neon loops with a white core, glow on the active edge, and 3×3 cards that read like hardware modules. Traditional holds a steady teal; Overclock burns orange/amber; Blind Node sinks into fog indigo; Corrupted flashes warning amber; Blackout bleeds electric purple; Fuzzy flickers gold; Async vibrates magenta; Decrypt reveals tangerine; Blitz Clock pulses mint.

You do not only solve the puzzle, you feel the protocol through the spectrum.

ARCADE — WHEN THE RULE BENDS

Same Slitherlink geometry. Completely different pressure (practice — no global ranking):
  • Blitz Clock — second economy: clean edges buy time; mistakes bill hard
  • Blind Node — fog of war: remember what the light already showed
  • Corrupted Sectors — fake clues; isolate the anomaly without buying the lie
  • Overclock — 120 seconds and a HUD that turns into urgency: close the loop before cut
  • Blackout — clues become dice; flip, read, remap under glitch
  • Fuzzy Logic — masked expressions (>=2, parity…); collapse the uncertainty
  • Async Mirroring — dual mirrored shards; synchronize the impossible
  • Decrypt — saturated grid: only subtract edges until the true loop remains

LEARN & TRAIN · GLOBAL CIRCUITS

Train without ranked heat in LEARN & TRAIN: How to Play, Calibration, Warmup, Lessons (watch), and Logic Drills.

Then hit RANKED // GLOBAL CIRCUITS:
  • Grid Gauntlet — Saturday UTC; three stages 5×5 Easy → 10×10 Normal → 15×15 Hard; shared timer; weekly Steam leaderboard
  • The Megaloop — last Sunday UTC of the month; 20×20 HARD; monthly Steam leaderboard
  • Throne Rush — monthly 15-country map; claim thrones under Limit time; Overlord name on the crown (playtest)

THE SCORE — LOOP-SYNTHWAVE OUTRUN

Analog bass, neon pads, night-race drums. Every protocol carries its own frequency: Traditional cruises the late hours; Overclock heats the circuit; Blitz counts time in BPM. The Command Deck pulses with the spectrum.

WHAT IS LIVE

  • Today's Puzzle — 9 ranked modes/day, 3 tries, per-mode Steam leaderboards
  • Global leaderboards with server-side anti-cheat validation
  • LEARN & TRAIN — Warmup, Lessons, Logic Drills
  • ARCADE — eight live mutations, each with color + challenge
  • Grid Gauntlet, The Megaloop, and Throne Rush — ranked circuits
  • Terminal UI synthwave/outrun, keyboard-first
  • Steam Deck playable at 1280×800
  • Accessibility — high contrast, reduce motion, focus audio mode

STILL IN THE LAB (ROADMAP)

Not promised in playtest / day one — shown in the menu as SOON or in development.
  • Arena Lightning Rounds / Days of Thunder (PvP)
  • Norms / title progression UI

NO ADS. NO IAP. NO BATTLE PASS.
Closed the loop? Submit. Compare. Come back tomorrow — nine fresh races will already be waiting.

Your deck is the board

An 8x8 board of gems and an hourglass that is already running. Drag across gems of the same colour, three or more, diagonals count, and let go to pop them for SHARDS × MULT. Bring the chain back to the gem you started on and you close a LOOP: every gem inside erupts with it. Beat the gate's target before the sand runs out.

Every coin is a choice

Between gates, the shop opens. Recruit ushabti, crack open packs, buy papyri and rites, or reroll and gamble on something better. Money is scarce and every slot in your row counts, so every purchase is a decision about the run you are building.

Rip it open

Packs are where a run turns. Tear open an Ushabti, Royal or Grand pack, pick the servant you want, and it joins your row for free. Papyrus, Constellation and Rites packs do the same for papyri, cluster levels and rites. The legendaries never come in a pack: fill the Eye of Horus, or find the right rite, and one of them might answer.

149 servants that work for you

In ancient Egypt, ushabti were small clay figures buried with the dead, so they could do the work of the afterlife in their owner's place. Here, they work for you. Each one reads your chain differently: how long it was, what colour, whether it closed, which relic it swallowed. Some add, some multiply, some grow with every pop. Put them in the right order and watch the whole row fire, one after another.

149 ushabti across four rarities, 11 of them legendary.

Blessed by the gods

Any ushabti can carry the blessing of a god, and each blessing changes how it scores.

  • Ptah's Gilding: +6 Shards for every gem in the chain

  • Khonsu's Gleam: +4 Mult

  • Ra's Radiance: ×1.5 Mult

  • Nut's Embrace: takes no room in your row

The gods change the rules

Every dynasty ends with a god, and the gods don't play fair. SERKET poisons a gem that burns your whole pop. ISFET shuffles the board every eight seconds. HEKA hides your time and your target inside a mirage. ANUBIS gives you ten pops, no more. 20 bosses and 5 final guardians wait across eight dynasties, and you see which god is coming before you shop.

Relics fall onto the board

22 relics in six families, and none of them sit in an inventory. They drop onto the board like gems. Chain one and it fires: beams across rows and columns, blasts that clear a whole area, seconds back on the hourglass. Catch two in the same chain and they combo.

One tomb. One run.

  • 8 gem enhancements: Faience doubles your Mult and might shatter, Wild joins any colour, Gold pays you for leaving it on the board

  • 23 papyri and 27 rites that rewrite the board

  • 11 clusters to level up, three of them hidden until you stumble onto them

  • 24 tags, 32 vouchers and 15 starting pouches

  • 8 stakes, from SAND down to DUAT, and an Endless mode that keeps the sand falling for as long as your engine holds

Welcome to LYSSA: Goddess of Rage, a tactical card RPG set in a world run by mercenaries, where three factions are locked in war and every fight is short, sharp, and brutal.

Pick Your Favorites. Make Them Unstoppable.

In LYSSA, every mercenary has a price — and a past. Recruit the ones you trust, gear them up, and turn them into legends. Then let your Commander tie it all together: their skills power up your whole deck, opening thousands of possible combinations to build a squad that fits your playstyle.

Grow Strong. Then Prove It.

Follow the twist-filled story campaign of LYSSA: Goddess of Rage and adapt to arenas where random obstacles change every fight. Then comes the true test: real-time PvP. Climb the ranked ladder, jump into battles and tournaments, and fight your way to the top of the leaderboards.
Play at your own pace: quick bursts or marathon sessions — how you get there is up to you. Just make sure you get there first.

Find Your Crew. Take the City.

Join an alliance, swap strategies with players from around the world, and team up for community events. Then go to war together: seize territory alongside your alliance and hold it against everyone who wants it back. In LYSSA: Goddess of Rage, the city belongs to whoever takes it.

Get Close. Get Personal.

Off the battlefield, your mercenaries have plenty to say. Chat with them, get to know the stories behind their contracts, and build relationships that unlock exclusive moments in your personal gallery.

So hire your mercenaries, build a deck no one sees coming, and fight your way to the top of a city that belongs to whoever takes it — your story in LYSSA: Goddess of Rage starts now!

A perforated chassis, a box of parts, and a robot that has to roll. You bolt the mechanics underneath, you wire the electrics on top, you switch it on — and then you find out what you got wrong.

Build with real parts

Solenoids, gears from 8 to 32 teeth, connecting rods, crank pins, bearings, shafts, drive wheels, flywheels, a contact breaker, capacitors, resistors, switches, relays, DC motors, transistors. Every part has a data sheet, real dimensions and a place where it fits. Nothing snaps magically into position: if your two shafts sit a few millimetres too far apart, the gears will not mesh, and the game will tell you by how much.

Nothing is faked

Ten thousand times a second, the game solves a real system of equations to find the voltage at every point of your build and the current in every wire. That is why your machine behaves like a machine. It stalls at dead centre until you fit a flywheel. Your breaker contacts erode spark by spark until they stop conducting — and a capacitor in the right place will save them. The connecting rod tears off if you stretch the linkage too far.

Every failure has a cause, and you can find it

Press F1 and the Encyclopaedia opens: every part, every idea, every fault, cross-referenced. Not a manual — a workshop notebook that explains why the spark eats your contacts, and what a magnetic field has to do with any of it.

What is in the game today

Forty-five build missions across four projects:

  • The robot vacuum, 32 missions. From a solenoid you slide by hand to a machine with motors, a brushroll, bumpers and relays that finds its own way. Then you take it home: the hallway, then the kitchen with its chairs to get around, a map of what is still dirty and your best time for each room.
  • The pinball table, 5 missions. An electromechanical table to build, then to play.
  • The dart machine, 5 missions. A 1980s bar machine: it hits nothing, it reads. Rectifier, filtering, regulator, matrix.
  • The electronics workshop, 3 missions. A new bench to learn transistors. This is the youngest project.

And a free sandbox with the parts box open.

The demo stays free

It holds the first twelve robot missions and the pinball table. If you are not sure, start there.

Eight languages

English, French, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Simplified Chinese, German and Japanese — every text of the game and every page of the Encyclopaedia. Everything beyond French and English was translated by an AI, with the vocabulary of the workshop, and no native speaker has read it yet: if a sentence sounds wrong, say so in the game's message board or on the forum, and it will be fixed.

You tried to sell a counterfeit antiquity to the wrong wizard. Now you're trapped in his maze — along with every other fool who crossed him.

Fight, scavenge, and outwit your opponents — or team up and conquer the dungeon together. Over 120 types of weapons, armor, and magical items are scattered throughout the maze, and every maze is different. Grab what you can, kill who you must, and be the last one out.

Legendary artifacts are drawn from world mythology — Norse, Greek, Egyptian, and more. Find one and it changes the fight.

Play the full Battle Royale game solo against cunning AI bots — no lobby, no matchmaking, no waiting. Or jump into multiplayer with up to 10 players in Battle Royale or Dungeon Co-op mode. Full support for controllers, keyboard, mouse, and touch.

A seed-driven roguelike deckbuilder about looting a sinking wreck with up to three friends and getting out while there's still a way back.

Every dive starts with a seed. Every seed builds the same waters for everyone who runs it. Go alone, or bring a crew and split the risk.

One wreck is never the whole run. The water is always rising.

Build the Deck as You Dive
You don't plan a build between runs, you find one. Cards come off the map as you push deeper into the wreck, and salvage cards modify what you already hold, turning a hand you settled for into a hand you meant to have.

Chart the Crossing
A run is a voyage, not a single dive. Clear what's guarding the wreck and you surface with a choice: where to sail next. Every stretch of water has its own character, its own wrecks, and its own way of killing you, from silt-choked shallows to trenches where the light gives out. The route is yours to pick, and two crews can share a seed and still come home with completely different stories.

The Tide Takes the Floor
The wreck floods one tile at a time. Flooded ground doesn't stop you, it just costs you, and every step through it takes a bite out of your health. Early on there's always a dry way around. Later there isn't, and the walk back to the surface is a bill you pay in blood. The question is never whether you can reach the exit. It's how much of you arrives.

The Hard Way Pays Better
Some parts of a wreck are sealed off, and you can always walk past them. Getting in takes the right tool card and puts you somewhere more dangerous than the route you skipped. It's also where the treasure and the rarest cards are. Every locked space is the same question: is this worth what it might cost your crew?

Your Tools Come Back With You
Tools are the one thing a run doesn't take from you. Everything else goes back to the sea, but the tools you recover stay in your kit, which means the next wreck opens up in ways the last one couldn't.

Every Run Has a Name
Runs are generated from a seed you can read, share, and challenge someone else to beat. Type a wreck's name into the Drowned Register and dive the exact same waters your friend just barely escaped: same rooms, same monsters, same tide. Compare hauls. Argue about who got greedy.

Four Divers, One Tide
Co-op for up to four. Spread out across the decks to cover more ship before the water rises, or stay tight and survive longer. The tide doesn't care how you split up.

You don't start behind the gate. You are the horde that breaks it.
Lairs & Lordships is a reverse tower defense strategy game. Plan the assault, break the keep, claim the land, then hold it when the kingdom wants it back.

PLAN THE ASSAULT, WAVE BY WAVE


Seven monster classes, one budget per wave: 150, then 125, then 100 army points. Use it or lose it. Skeletons up front, Golems as walls that walk, Orcs to break the real ones, casters behind. Once sent, a wave fights on its own; between waves, the battle freezes while you plan the next.

SEVEN FORTRESSES, SEVEN RULES

Kill the lookout before the horn sounds. Spring the forest ambush with a front line. Smash the rockfall for a back road. Split your wave before the volley battery picks a flank. Hit harder on hot ground, and burn for it. Wade the flooding ford, or take the bridge. Draw the royal reserve to one flank, then hit the other.

ELITES AND CHAMPIONS


Watch for gold rings. Elites carry up to three passives, from War Banner to Last Stand. On Difficulty III, twelve named champions join them, one to three per fortress. Click any unit to read its card, then break the aura carriers first.

BREAK THE KEEP, CLAIM THE LAND


Take a fortress and its keep sinks. Your lair rises where it stood, and the land pays you gold: spend it on five more monster classes and 89 monster upgrades, or on your lairs, for the day you defend them.

THE KINGDOM WANTS IT BACK


The first raid comes straight to your gates. After that, the more you take, the angrier the kingdom gets: raids grow larger and tougher, and up to two can stand at once while you conquer, three once the whole map is yours. Every raid brings elites of its own.

NOW BE THE WALL

Every lair starts with 60 wall segments, and lair upgrades add more. Draw a corridor and build towers at its mouth. Then defend in person, leave a defense plan for the garrison, or strike first: take the fortress where a raid musters before it marches. Lose, and the land is Lost until you storm it back.

SCROLLS AND SIDE EXPEDITIONS


Aim a Fireball where the crowd is thickest. Craft all six scrolls at the Scroll workshop, and set runes in them.

Dig the Ore Vein and search the Ancient Ruins for what the workshop needs. Or take a bandit camp with one army, 100 points and no reinforcements.

FEATURES

  • 7 monster classes, 89 monster upgrades, 13 of them abilities that trigger on their own
  • 7 fortresses, 7 rules, 3 difficulty levels each, on a map that forks twice
  • 175 elites, 12 of them named champions, across the seven fortresses
  • 6 battle scrolls, 3 runes, 3 bandit camps
  • World events every few battles, and a short training battle with Abel, your advisor

Lakeside Idle is a cozy idle fishing game. Wait patiently for a bite, or use attacks and gear combinations to reel in fish more quickly.

【Relax by the Lake】

Enjoy peaceful moments by the water. Designed for idle play, the game is perfect for a quick break or as a calming desktop companion.

【Collect Fish】

Explore different seasons and times of day to catch common, rare, and even legendary fish. Record their star ratings, lengths, and weights as you complete your Fish Compendium.

【Mix and Match Gear】

Unlock fishing rods, floats, and bait. Combine gems with different effects to create your own fishing build.

【Four Seasons, Day and Night】

The lakeside scenery changes with the seasons and time of day. These changing conditions also affect which fish you can encounter.

【Key Features】

• Relaxing idle fishing
• A variety of fish to discover and collect
• Fishing rods, floats, bait, and gem combinations
• Different attack and progression builds
• Four seasons and a day-night cycle
• A cozy and calming desktop companion

You were once a young person exhausted by the daily grind.

After receiving news of your grandfather's passing, you quit your job and returned to the seaside town.

You inherited an old cafe filled with memories.

While you thought this was just a fresh start, while tidying up the shop...

You accidentally awakened "Lami," a robot girl left behind by your grandfather.

From that day on, you and Lami began your life together,

Facing the unsolved mysteries hidden behind this cafe.

Run the Cafe with Lami

Greet customers, prepare meals, and bring life back to this quiet old shop.

Adjust the layout, purchase furniture, and optimize the workflow.

Slowly transform the cafe into the space you’ve always dreamed of.

As business gets on track, more customers and stories will find their way into your shop.

Craft Equipment to Improve Efficiency

Running a cafe is about more than just serving coffee.

Gather materials and craft tools to make your work more efficient.

From simple upgrades to new devices that save you time,

Step by step, turn the old shop into a convenient and unique space.

Experience the Life of a Coder

As a former engineer, you’ll use your skills to solve problems.

Follow the music to complete challenges in rhythm-based gameplay.

Develop new features and repair broken systems.

Turn coding from a source of stress into a way to move the cafe forward.

Explore Beyond the Town with Lami

Beyond the cafe, even more places await your discovery.

Step outside the town with Lami to explore forests, lakesides, and unknown regions.

Search for materials, solve incidents, and gradually uncover the truth your grandfather left behind.

Some sights are beautiful, but some places are far from safe.

When strange lights appear in the sky, your peaceful life may be shattered by a sudden crisis.

Face Emergencies Side-by-Side

Lami is more than just a helper; she is a partner who ventures with you.

As the story unfolds, you will encounter haywire machines and sudden disasters,

Along with the troubles lurking behind the cafe.

Work together with Lami to protect the life you’ve worked so hard to build.

"Lami: A Cup of Code and Coffee" is a 3D casual game combining cafe management, crafting, exploration, rhythm gameplay, and story-driven adventure.

If you enjoy relaxing management and growing alongside characters while uncovering secrets,

Then this cafe is waiting for you to open its doors.

Wait.. YOU CAN DRIVE A ROAD IN THIS GAME?! AWESOME!

Yep, welcome to Lanelord!

A chaotic Road vs Car multiplayer experience.

In this game you can either play as a twisting road or a car that tries to survive by not falling to its doom.

  • Road Player: Turn and shape the lane in real time. You can either help your friend to stay on... or place deadly traps to shake it off!

  • Car Player: Your goal is to stay on the road, no matter what! Use your skill as a driver and items to help you on your way.

Game Modes

Solo Escort

You play the road and need to escort a car as far as you can! Can you push your highscore?

Co‑op Mode

Team up with one of your Friends or a complete stranger to get as far as possible!
Sync your rhythm and use items to help the other player survive.

Versus Mode

In this game mode the road feels an itch on its back... shake it off!
As the car you just need to survive longer than the road.
Items in this game mode either help you or hinder the other player to progress.
Use them wisely!

Ranked Mode

Compete with a random stranger in a 4 round match-up.
To balance things out between rounds you will switch roll with your opponent.
Can you achieve the title "LANELORD"?!

Online Multiplayer

Each 2-player game mode can be played online against strangers.
Either open a lobby, play a quick match, which will automatically throw you into a game or compete for higher ranks with ranked mode.

Items

Choose a loadout of 5 Items to assist you in your battle to stay alive!

There are multiple helpful, but fun Items.
You wanna blow up some trees? Got you!
Maybe you wanna smack your opponent with a hammer? Good!

Customization

Shape the look and color of your Road and Car to your liking.
But not so fast.. if you want to get the cool stuff, play the game!
Everything is unlock-able by just playing. 

Weather and Time of Day

Ever wanted to play in a foggy night, or a snowy winter wonderland? 

Each Biome has its own randomized weather and time of day. 

Features

  • Procedural generated biomes with randomly generated weather for each biome. No two games are the same!

  • Customization System to choose your look and item loadout

  • Ranked Mode to compete against other player

  • Player progression. Level up to earn new cosmetics!

  • Controller Support!

  • Steam Deck functionality! (Experimental, but tested by me!)

  • And endless fun!

Lanternfall is out now, and it will keep growing. We chose to release it as a complete game rather than in Early Access, so you get all fifteen realms from day one, with plenty of improvements and new content still to come.

The corruption beneath the harvest has awakened.

What begins in a familiar pumpkin patch leads through candlelit graveyards, crooked bridges, enchanted forests and increasingly impossible places. Every realm is a detailed animated gothic diorama, filled with flickering light, moving weather, hidden routes and enemies designed to test a different part of your defence.

Build an arsenal, not a disposable loadout

Towers you purchase enter your Tower Bank. Redeploy the towers you already own on later battlefields, improve them through multiple visible upgrade tiers, or sell them at a loss when a new strategy demands it. The choices made early in the campaign shape the resources and options available later.

Read the threat before the wave arrives

Enemy portraits reveal what is approaching and identify armour, immunity and movement type. Physical, fire, shock and magic attacks each have battles where they excel — and enemies that punish relying on only one answer. Aura towers, air threats and water routes keep each map tactically different.

Survive a campaign that keeps changing

Waves are authored as distinct tactical problems rather than repeated stat ramps. Gold does not come from kills alone: hire miners to work the ground behind your lines and they earn their cost back over many trips, so every hire is weighed against a tower you could build right now. Choose when to expand, when to upgrade, and when to send the next wave in early for bonus gold. Later realms demand that you balance immediate survival against the resources needed for the battles ahead.

A haunted world built to move

Lanterns flicker, shadows breathe, rain strengthens, rivers flow and the landscape reacts around the battle. Each realm has its own landmark, colour language, route design, ambient soundscape and Halloween identity while remaining part of one connected journey.

Key features

  • A fifteen-level gothic Halloween campaign.
  • A persistent Tower Bank that carries owned towers and upgrades forward.
  • A gold economy of real decisions: hire miners that pay back over time, or call the next wave in early for a bonus.
  • Distinct physical, fire, shock, magic, air and aura strategies.
  • Four visible upgrade tiers for the starting tower set.
  • Ground, flying and water-route enemies with armour and immunity counters.
  • Hand-authored waves, bosses and economy choices rather than repeated stat ramps.
  • Animated 3D-rendered battlefields with dynamic lighting, weather and sound.
  • Central audio mixing with separate music, ambience and effects controls.

Are you sure you want to press that choice?

`Last Choice Hero` is a choice-driven dark comedy adventure game about a boy chosen to be the hero, only to have his fate twisted by the very choices that were supposed to save the world.

The king calls you.

You set out to defeat the Demon Lord.

You gather allies, help people in need, and make the right choices.

...At least, that is how it is supposed to go. Unfortunately, the choices in this world are usually mean.

The action that looks right at first glance may lead to the worst possible ending.

A ridiculous option may somehow bring you closer to the heart of the story.

You may try to save the world and end up ruining someone's life instead.

Players progress through the hero's journey by reading short scenes, examining the screen, and choosing what to do next.

As you collect a long list of BAD ENDs, you will gradually move closer to the truth behind this world.

The main story has 16 stages.

There are 42 endings to discover.

The fun is not only in finding the correct answer.

It is also in watching what happens when you press a choice.

And in finding out just how awful the result can get.

The cast includes a hero, a queen, a golden slime, a black knight, an ice princess, a fire prince, a witch, a warrior, a goddess, and many other characters with dangerously strong personalities.

In a world that looks like a classic RPG, slightly dark, slightly stupid, and sometimes strangely lingering choices are waiting for you.

Beyond the main story, there are also post-clear elements such as an ending gallery, character collection, afterstories, and a survivor-style bonus mode.

This is not a game about saving the world in a clean, satisfying way.

It is a game where you press choices you do not want to press, witness endings you do not want to see, and still feel tempted to peek at the next option.

Hero.

Are you really sure about that choice?

Protect the flame. Build a home. Pass on its stories.

Tend a small village by day and defend its people and flame by night. Residents’ lives become books, and journeys leave memories in journals. Build, defend, and shape a village whose stories connect one generation to the next.





Screens show the full game under development (Japanese UI). They do not establish that all shown features are included in the currently distributed demo.




Build homes and workplaces around the last flame. Turn today’s resources into daily life—and preparations for the night ahead.


Captured during isolated play in the development build.

Build by day. Defend by night.

Gather wood, stone, and food. Build homes, farms, workshops, and defenses. Residents' work, hunger, stamina, hauling, and building use affect one another. Prepare fences and gates and assign a night watch before the Shadows arrive. Damage and shortages carry into the next morning.







Your daytime preparations shape the coming night. Approaching Shadows, dwindling fuel and damaged defenses: deciding who goes where can make the next morning possible.


Captured during isolated play in the development build.

Start your first village in the free demo

The free demo is available now. Use the demo download on this page to experience gathering, construction, research, night defense, repairs, rebuilding, and the demo loop of records and inheritance.

Revisit each resident’s life, one book at a time

The work that sustained the village. A first encounter. A night spent guarding the flame. In the full game under development, choose residents’ records from a bookshelf and look back on their lives. When a village falls, carry its records and memories into the next civilization.


Actual development-build UI (Japanese interface, test save). This is not a naturally progressed playthrough and does not establish availability in the currently distributed demo.

Guide a small settlement into its next age


From wood to stone and brick, develop your village’s buildings and defenses. Work toward Day 100 and the legacy you will pass on.




Actual rendering of stone and brick defenses. This development-build display test uses staged construction states, not naturally reached progress.

Cave of Echoes: follow the light beyond the village


Explore while watching your light, food and health. Venture one step deeper, or return with your discoveries? Preparations in the village support a new adventure.




Actual development-build screen from a test save, with cave access and supplies staged for interaction testing.

Eastern Journey: returning travelers reveal the world


Returning travelers’ reports lift the fog on the world map. Develop surveyed routes into contact outposts and pass exploration records to the next village.




Actual development-build screen from a test save, with a prepared expedition and a verified return. Not naturally reached progression.


These are highlights of the full game under development. Additional full-game features such as the cave, journey, and world map are not a statement of what is included in the currently available demo.

From Early Access toward the full release

We plan to keep improving long-term balance, controls, readability, buildings, research, calamities, record events, and supported languages. Content and implementation order may change with testing and feedback.

What will your village leave for the next civilization? Play now in Early Access, or add the game to your wishlist to follow future updates.

As a weary contract killer in a dark cyberpunk underground, you must complete your final contract. You have to find a way to survive by defeating the enemies you face.

Gameplay Last Contract is a fast-paced 2D action game with a one-hit kill mechanic. With both you and your enemies dying in a single strike, you must rely on your reflexes to survive. Deflect bullets with your katana, close the distance with your dash ability, and eliminate enemies with your shuriken attacks.

About Last Contract The game focuses entirely on pure action with its pixel art style and cyberpunk atmosphere. There are no complex skill trees or grinding systems; there is only you, your weapons, and your reflexes.

Key Features:

  • Unforgiving one-hit kill combat system

  • 2D pixel art style and neon cyberpunk atmosphere

  • Melee combat and bullet deflection mechanics with a katana

  • Dash ability for instant repositioning

  • Shurikens for long-range attacks

  • 8-bit retro sound effects

  • Challenging progression based purely on skill and reflexes

THE LAST LIGHT BEFORE KNOWN SPACE RUNS OUT


You arrived broke and owing Calder for repairs. Now the ship is yours, the tab is open, and the Last Exit Diner is the one neutral light at the edge of a frontier held together by trade lanes, old grudges, and ancient Progenitor gates.

Edge of Known Space is a single-player 2D space-action RPG about keeping a battered ship flying, taking dangerous jobs, and uncovering why rogue Progenitor machines are multiplying across inhabited space.

FLY THE FRONTIER


  • Pilot a momentum-driven ship through toroidal combat spaces where position, approach, and escape routes matter.
  • Fight raiders, rogue firewalls, and self-replicating Progenitor viruses with primary weapons, secondary systems, tractor tools, and consumable repairs.
  • Use trade lanes to travel between planets and ancient Prog Tech warpgates to cross between star systems.
  • Form up with Calder, freighters, and mission convoys, then break formation when an ambush turns the route into a battlefield.

THE DINER IS HOME


Every run begins and ends at the Last Exit Diner. Collect payment, repair and refuel, manage your ship and cargo, listen to the jukebox, and choose the next job from the board. The Diner is more than a station: it is a strange fixed point in a network that should not still work.

CHOOSE WHO ARRIVED


Start as a Hauler, Ex-Enforcer, Fugitive, Colonist, Corporate Defector, or Void-Born pilot. Your origin changes your opening resources, first upgrade, and the way Calder and Gary frame your arrival without locking the campaign behind reputation choices.

FOLLOW THE MISSING SIGNAL


Routine work begins to expose a larger theft: pieces of the Last Exit Engine have been scattered through the gate network, and each fragment still changes the space around it. Recover them before corporations, raiders, and the machines behind the gates decide what the Last Exit should become.

Keep the ship moving. Pay the tab. Do not ask Gary why the bathroom door opens where it does.

about_html:
The Whiteout swallowed the outer settlements. One armoured train still runs the Endless Rail Circuit, carrying supplies, survivors, and fifty varieties of deeply questionable advertising.

Keep the Last Train Moving


Last Exit Diner: The Last Train is a fast six-minute rail-survival game. Your five wagons are the line between a hungry sky and the Last Exit. Automatic roof guns hold the swarm back, but the train's enormous Dreadnought cannon answers directly to you.

  • Man the Dreadnought. Hold to traverse its six barrels and central cannon shot across the battlefield.
  • Defend five individual wagons. Every surviving wagon earns a mastery star at the end of the route.
  • Fight a hostile flying ecosystem. Swarms overwhelm, latchers disable roof guns, chargers hit hard, and screamers strengthen everything around them.
  • Choose your build on the move. Rail upgrades arrive roughly every 30 seconds, mixing permanent refits, consumable countermeasures, bombs, and specialized ammunition.
  • Cross ten escalating biomes. Each route brings its own scenery, hazards, enemies, starting speed, and health pressure.
  • Chase the Last Exit. Survive the six-minute run, protect every wagon, and turn bounty into local high-score glory.

Keep it moving. Keep the guns firing. Reach the Last Exit.

Build the maze. Survive the night. Repeat.

Choose your garden gnome, pick your weapons, and defend your shrines against the forces of evil in this cartoon maze-building tower defense roguelite. Each gnome comes with different stat bonuses and penalties. Fight through the night, then spend your resources on upgrades and new flower towers before the next wave arrives.

  • Build your own maze. Place flower towers and barricades to shape enemy routes and funnel the hordes into choke points.

  • Death isn’t the end. Your Life Keeper Shrine brings fallen gnomes back into battle. Protect it: if it falls and no gnomes remain alive, your run is over.

  • Survive as long as you can. Face increasingly difficult nights in endless survival. How long will your defenses hold?

  • Adapt to every run. Random drops expand your starting options, while changing enemy combinations keep you experimenting with new builds.

  • Face a boss every five waves. Randomly selected bosses put your maze and your build to the test.

  • Protect your source of power. Each of your three shrines offers its own kind of support, from revival to choosing bonuses and penalties before each wave, or doubling—even tripling—your collected resources.

  • Keep growing stronger. Upgrade your gnome’s stats, weapons, towers, potions, and shrines. Many upgrades have no level cap.

  • Fight alongside your towers. Your weapons fire automatically, letting you focus on movement, positioning, and keeping enemies away from your shrines. Use potions for temporary boosts.

  • Unlock more ways to play. Earn new gnomes, weapons, towers, and potion recipes through permanent progression across runs.

  • Play solo or with friends. Defend the garden together in local co-op for up to four players.

RUN FOR YOUR LIFE

The rooftops are collapsing. The horde is closing in. Your friends are absolutely not helping.

Last Man Running is a fast, physical rooftop elimination runner. Build momentum across procedural routes while a 240-zombie horde erases every mistake.


KEEP MOVING

  • Vault, slide, wall-run, wall-jump, grab ledges, and double-jump to stay ahead.
  • Smash through props and hazards across changing rooftop courses.
  • Tackle, grab, spin, shield, and throw other runners off the safest line.

PLAY ELIMINATION, CO-OP, OR SOLO

  • Elimination: tackle, grab and throw your rivals in free-for-all or team matches. Battle locally or online to become the last runner standing.
  • Co-op: stick together and outrun the horde, locally or online.
  • Solo: chase a high score with momentum multipliers, pickups, and two banked respawns.
  • Mix couch and remote runners in the same online session.

FIGHT DIRTY

A clean line is good. Ruining someone else’s is better. Charge a tackle, drag a downed rival, use another runner as a shield, or throw them straight into trouble.

FEATURES

  • Procedurally assembled rooftops with alternate routes, hazards, breakable scenery, and startled pigeons.
  • Quick Play, public and friends-only Steam lobbies, invites, and relay networking for online co-op and PvP.
  • 20 Steam Achievements tied to movement, survival, destruction, and glorious bad behavior.
  • Gritty low-poly, PS1-inspired cityscapes packed with neon, rust, grime, and industrial danger.

Keep moving. Fight dirty. Try not to become lunch.

Last Offer: Car Dealer is an open-world car trading and dealership simulation game.

Explore the city, discover vehicles for sale, inspect their condition, negotiate with owners, and decide whether a deal is actually worth your money. Bring the cars you buy back to your dealership, prepare them for sale, and wait for the right customer.

A cheap car is not always a good deal. An expensive car is not always a bad investment.

Learn the market, understand your customers, and know when to walk away.

Find, Inspect and Negotiate

Drive through the open world and discover cars that are up for sale.

Check their mileage, condition, and market value before making an offer. Negotiate with the seller and try to get the best possible price.

One bad purchase can wipe out your profit.

Build and Grow Your Dealership

Your dealership is more than just a place to park cars.

Fill your showroom with vehicles, organize your stock, and gradually turn a small business into a larger and more professional dealership.

As your business grows, new opportunities become available.

Negotiate With Customers

Customers can visit your dealership, walk around the showroom, and inspect the vehicles that interest them.

They may ask questions about a car, request information, and negotiate the price with you.

Not every customer will buy.

Sometimes letting a customer walk away is better than accepting a bad deal.

Customize Your Cars

Give your vehicles their own character before putting them up for sale.

Modify their appearance, customize different parts, and create cars that stand out from the rest of your stock.

Some modifications may make a vehicle more attractive to buyers, while others are simply about creating something that fits your own style.

Drive Through an Open World

Your business does not exist inside a menu.

Drive the cars you purchase, explore the city, and travel between your dealership, workshops, and other locations yourself.

The vehicles you trade are also the vehicles you drive.

The Hidden Side of the Business

Not every opportunity in the city is completely legal.

Certain unusual and restricted vehicles can take you beyond ordinary dealership business.

Meetings may happen at different locations and at specific times. Buying the vehicle is only the beginning — getting it safely back to your own garage can also be part of the deal.

Higher risk can mean higher profit.

If you make it back.

Buy low. Negotiate hard. Sell smart.

Every negotiation has an ending.

Make yours the Last Offer.

Two balls. Twelve paddles. No mercy.

Last Paddle Standing! is a chaotic multiplayer arcade game about one very simple thing: don't let the ball get past you.

Up to 12 players surround an ever-changing arena. Return the ball, survive the chaos, and be the last paddle standing. Every elimination shrinks the arena, speeds up the rallies, and makes the survivors increasingly uncomfortable.

Score goals and survive arenas to earn points. The most points wins the match, and the last survivor takes the Last Paddle Standing title.

And getting eliminated doesn't mean you're done causing problems.

Short Matches. Maximum Chaos.

Jump in, play a few rounds, leave happy. Most matches wrap up in under 15 minutes, depending on player count and the rules you pick.

Customize your look, grab your favorite paddle, and you're in; everything is playable from the first match. No grind. Just return the ball.

1v1 With a Friend? 12-Player Free-for-All?

Play a clean 1v1, dive into a chaotic free-for-all, or team up in pairs and trios.

  • Free-for-all: 2–12 players, every paddle for itself.

  • Pairs: 4–12 players in teams of two.

  • Trios: 6, 9 or 12 players in teams of three.

Teammates share one goal and defend it together from stacked rails, one in front of the other.

Want a five-player match? Go for it.

Want all twelve players squeezed into one arena? Terrible idea. Do it anyway.

Create lobbies and tweak the rules, hit Quick Play to find a match, or fill the empty spots with bots.

One Couch. Twelve Players.

No need to go online: up to 12 players can play together on one screen, in any mode. Grab a controller, press a button, and you're in. Keyboard and mouse players are welcome too, and every seat can rebind its own controls.

Got a friend or two on the couch? Take them into online lobbies as well: two local players play as a pairs team, three as a trios team.

The Arena Doesn't Stay the Same

Players don't simply disappear when they're eliminated - the arena changes with them. As players get knocked out, the arena rebuilds itself around whoever is still alive, shrinking and shifting shape as the match progresses. A huge, chaotic arena can end as a very uncomfortable little 1v1.

Hosts pick one of three arena layouts:

  • Symmetrical: the classic read. Equal goals on an even court.

  • Asymmetrical: equal goals, uneven outer walls and strange bank angles.

  • Chaotic: uneven walls plus randomly placed internal barriers. Play the bounce.

Survive Long Enough to Get Stronger

Every paddle plays differently. Pick one of nine sizes, and one of twelve starting abilities.

Passive abilities:

  • English: spin builds through the rally and adds speed off obstacles and inner walls.

  • Powerhouse: harder returns; centered hits turn spin into raw speed.

  • Velcro: catch the ball, hold it for a beat, then send it back with your spin.

  • Slingshot: keep moving to charge a harder-hitting return.

  • Shark: fast, heavy and momentum-driven; your paddle shrinks as you slow down.

  • Last Stand: down to your final life? Longer, snappier paddle.

Active abilities:

  • Dash: burst along your edge; balls you sweep up take maximum spin.

  • Magnet: drag nearby balls toward the middle of your paddle.

  • Nova: shove nearby balls away.

  • Cold Snap: charge your next return; the side it hits slows down for 6 seconds.

  • Split Shot: your next return splits into two balls.

  • Bulwark: raise a one-hit barrier across your goal.

As the field thins out, the survivors draft perks and abilities mid-match.

Your Rules

Hosts can fine-tune every match with rule presets or build their own house rules from scratch.

Or go custom: set lives, goal width, obstacle pacing, curveballs, draft timing, allowed abilities and perks.

Eliminated? Good. Get Revenge.

Getting knocked out isn't fun... unless you can make everyone else's game worse.

Eliminated players return as malicious spirits and keep participating from beyond the grave. Spawn obstacles, interfere with rallies, and make life miserable for the players rude enough to survive longer than you.

  • Place obstacles: Pillar, Vortex, Wormhole, Orbiting Moons, Goalie Drone and Spore.

  • Upgrade them: a pillar that moves, a vortex that turns into a black hole, a goalie drone that becomes the GOAT, and more.

  • Throw a curveball: make every ball hiccup, freeze for a showdown shot, or dance to the beat.

  • Hinder a survivor: Reverse Controls, Oversteer, Mini or Heavy Hands.

You might be out. Your revenge isn't.

Key Features

  • Online multiplayer for 2–12 players, from tense 1v1 duels to total 12-player chaos

  • Local multiplayer for up to 12 players on one screen, plus up to three couch players in online lobbies

  • Free-for-all (2–12), pairs (4–12) and trios (6, 9 or 12)

  • Quick Play matchmaking, public and friends-only custom lobbies, and bots in four difficulties

  • An arena that shrinks and reshapes itself with every elimination

  • Three arena layouts: Symmetrical, Asymmetrical and Chaotic

  • Twelve starting abilities, nine paddle sizes, and mid-match drafts with seven perks

  • Rule presets plus fully custom house rules

  • Keep playing after elimination as a malicious spirit: place obstacles, throw curveballs and hinder the living

  • Fast matches, usually under 15 minutes

  • Cosmetic customization, no grind

  • Gamepad support for Xbox, PlayStation, Switch Pro and more via Steam Input

《Last Ride》 is a first-person adventure of paranormal suspense about investigating and capturing spirits. You step in as a rookie investigator at the agency and enter anomalous sites where spirits lie hidden. You explore the scene yourself, search for every trace, examine clues that should not be there, and determine the kind of spirit before you. Then you follow the rules that apply to that spirit alone, and by those rules you track it, weaken it, and capture it.

Story

The protagonist's younger sister runs a paranormal agency. Lately, she tells the protagonist that a supernatural curse has settled on her, and that she can no longer run the agency. For her sake, the protagonist takes the agency over and looks for a way to lift the curse. Each time a case is cleared, the sister draws the spirit of that case back from the supernatural dimension. The curse does not lift. It passes to the protagonist. At the end, the protagonist returns to the original courtyard, seeking a means of redemption.

The Beginning

The game starts when an assignment comes in. The assignment leads you into an unfamiliar place. Switch on your flashlight, make a first survey, learn the site, and collect as much information as you can.

The Investigation

When a supernatural spirit shows itself, evade its pursuit. While you do, gather what you can of its story and its motive. Look for a way to counter it, or help it fulfill its wish. Once the spirit is restrained, open your camera, center it in the frame, and take the photograph that seals it.

Containment

When the assignment is finished, a portal takes you back to the agency. Contain the spirit in a special vessel.

Every spirit carries an obsession of its own. To redeem them is to redeem yourself.

THE LAST SHUTTLE WON'T WAIT

LAST SHUTTLE is an online co-op and competitive action-adventure for 2 to 4 players.

Fight your way through dangerous ruins filled with hostile creatures, locked doors, and traps. Collect keys to unlock doors and reach the last shuttle before the opposing team.

PLAY TOGETHER WITH 2 TO 4 PLAYERS

In 2- or 3-player matches, AI-controlled robots fill the open robot slots and support each team's fighter.

In a 4-player match, two teams face off in 2v2 competition. Each team consists of a fighter and a robot. Because the two roles have different abilities, victory depends on how well you work with your partner.

TWO ROLES, ONE TEAM

  • THE FIGHTER

Navigate dangerous terrain, defeat enemies in close combat, and collect keys to clear a path to escape.

  • THE ROBOT

Stay close to your partner, dash toward enemies and obstacles, knock down the opposing fighter to slow their advance, and activate your partner's shield in moments of danger.

Neither role can handle every situation alone. Combine their different abilities with precise timing to become a truly effective team.

COOPERATE, COMPETE, AND ESCAPE

Monsters and environmental hazards threaten everyone equally, but only one team can win.

Protect your partner and move forward together. At the right moment, disrupt the opposing team and create an opportunity to escape first.

Simply reaching the end is not enough. You have to get there before your opponents.

KEY FEATURES

• Online play for 2 to 4 players

• AI robots that fill open slots in 2- and 3-player matches

• Competition ranging from 1v1 matches to role-based 2v2 team play

• Two distinct roles: the fighter and the robot

• Close-range action combat against a variety of enemies as the fighter

• Robot abilities including dashes, obstacle destruction, rival knockdowns, and partner shield activation

• Keys, checkpoints, locked doors, and a variety of traps

• In-game voice chat with general and team channels

• Character skins and expressive emotes

FIGHT THROUGH YOUR ENEMIES. OUTRUN YOUR RIVALS.

DON'T MISS THE LAST SHUTTLE.

GO LIVE. GET OUT ALIVE.

You and up to three friends are streamers chasing the one video that blows up: a night inside a house nobody has entered in twenty years. The camera is rolling, the chat is watching, and something in the house is watching too.

ONE SEES IT. ONE SOLVES IT.

The clues to every puzzle only appear inside the ghost's room. One player stays in there, describing what glows on the walls, while the others work the puzzle on the far side of the house. Sixty seconds on the clock, the ghost hunting all of you, and proximity voice means you have to shout to be heard.

THE HOUSE REMEMBERS

The ghost is held to the house by its memories. Find the room where it is strongest, follow the clues, and solve the puzzles hidden in its old belongings. Every memory you restore shows you a piece of who it was.

THE CHAT SEES EVERYTHING

Your stream is live the whole time. Viewers react to every shadow, every scream and every mistake. The closer the ghost gets, the more people tune in.

IT HUNTS

Each clue you return makes the ghost stronger and more visible. The lights flicker, the doors open, and then it comes for you. You can't fight it. Run, hide in a wardrobe or under a bed, and hold your breath.

FEATURES

  • 1–4 player online co-op, or go in alone

  • A living stream: live chat, viewers and your own camera inside the game

  • A ghost with a story: investigate its memories and solve the puzzles they hide

  • Hunts you can't fight: run, hide and survive together

  • Customizable streamers and a garage base to plan your next broadcast

Only one survives. Will it be your build?

Enter the Last Warrior Arena, a fast-paced roguelike autobattler where strategy, planning, and smart decision-making determine your fate. Build your warrior, craft powerful synergies, and fight through relentless arena stages where every choice matters.

Prepare your character, then watch intense 1v1 battles unfold — victory depends not on reflexes, but on the strength of your strategy.

STORY

The arena was built to settle the wars of kings. Now the kings are dust, but the battles never end.

Warriors, monsters, and forgotten champions are drawn into its shifting realms, bound by one promise: the last warrior standing may claim their freedom.

You have entered to win. But with every fallen opponent, a question grows—who keeps the arena alive, and why are they so afraid to let you leave?

KEY FEATURES

  • Tactical 1v1 auto-battles — Your warrior fights automatically. Your choices determine how they fight.

  • A diverse roster of warriors — Explore different classes with their own abilities and playstyles.

  • Build-defining equipment — Combine weapons, armour, and accessories with unique skills.

  • Elemental synergies — Mix powers from different schools to create powerful combinations.

  • Choose your next-fight skills — Adapt your strategy before entering the arena.

  • Pick your opponents — Weigh enemy strengths against your build and choose your next challenge.

  • Powerful bosses — Put your build to the test against deadly foes across varied arenas.

  • Discover powerful Artifact Encounters — Choose between elemental artifacts with enhanced effects to strengthen your build and shape the rest of your run.

  • Roguelike progression — Unlock skills, strengthen your warrior, and explore new builds each run.
