LAST ZONE IS A BRUTAL CO-OP SURVIVAL GAME SET IN A POST-SOVIET WORLD.

The world has fallen into chaos, and every step is a fight for survival. Face hordes of mutants, ruthless factions, and a constant shortage of resources. Team up with friends, turn ruins into an impregnable fortress, craft equipment, and fight back against the wasteland itself.

Your goal is simple: survive, secure your place, and uncover what turned this world into hell.

Co-op in LAST ZONE is all about teamwork: while one player searches for supplies, another builds defenses, and a third fights off mutants. Only by working together can you transform ruins into a stronghold capable of resisting the horrors of the wasteland.

INFECTED ZONES ARE THE RICHEST — AND THE DEADLIEST

Infected zones are the richest — and the deadliest — places in the world. Face hordes of mutants with unique behaviors and abilities. Use tactics, monitor radiation levels, and always watch your corners: only those who stay alert survive here.

THE COUNTRYSIDE IS THE PERFECT PLACE TO HIDE. OR DIE.

Explore the haunting atmosphere of abandoned villages. Supplies are scarcer here than in the cities, and so are your chances of surviving alone. Fortify an old country house, fend off mutants in the fields, and use the terrain to protect your shelter. You are in charge here — until night falls.

BUILDING IS YOUR KEY TO SURVIVAL.

Gather resources, construct walls and defensive structures, and turn abandoned buildings into fortified bastions capable of withstanding mutant raids and unwanted visitors.

PANEL APARTMENT BLOCKS

These grim concrete labyrinths hide either valuable loot or certain death behind every apartment door. Search every floor, move carefully through the stairwells, and try not to get trapped inside these endless concrete boxes.

RIVERS AND LAKES ARE MORE THAN JUST SCENERY

They are also a source of food. Grab a fishing rod, find a quiet spot, and catch fish before the local creatures notice you. A peaceful fishing trip may be your only chance to rest and fill your stomach after another harsh day in the Zone.

DO NOT LOOK FOR EASY PATHS.

The best loot is hidden behind boarded-up windows and locked doors. Break your way inside to find truly valuable gear.

The Last Hope On Wheels

Civilization has fallen. Four powers carve up what's left: mutants, an alien hive, rogue machines — and raiders scavenging the scraps. The survivors are silent; the airwaves are dead. Your armored convoy is the first to go back on air. Every rescued survivor, every radio tower, every liberated territory gives a voice back to those still alive.

Build Your War Machine

Start with a locomotive. Add cars as you level up: turrets, cannons, tesla coils, mine layers, generators, repair and cargo cars. Recruit and train your crew. But the longer the convoy, the harder it is to control — and the more vulnerable it gets.

Every Car Counts

Each car has its own health. Take too much damage and the car breaks off, along with everything behind it. Enemies don't just shoot: some latch onto your cars and drag the convoy down, others hit you with harpoons. Scrape them off against obstacles — or watch your convoy grind to a halt.

Driving recklessly? Hit your own tail and you lose it. Masters use this to their advantage.

Hordes By The Thousand

Thousands of enemies advance as one solid front and flow around the convoy from both sides. The whole convoy opens up on them. Elites and bosses drop power-ups — brief, but enough to turn a fight.

Crew On Board

Rescued survivors don't sit at the base — they work right in the run. Gunners cover the sides, mechanics patch the cars, scavengers strip wrecks and tankers, observers spot threats early. Stop, drop your people, grab the loot — and get moving before the horde arrives. Ram a wreck and you get a pile of junk instead of loot.

Carve Your Path

Roads are fast. Off-road slows you down, rubble stops you cold. Wasteland, ice, swamps, dead forest — every biome has its own roads, its own obstacles and its own quirks. And gas stations, depots, factories and ruined cities are loot — if your crew has someone who can take it.

Take The Planet Back

The global map is your sandbox. Each hex is a sector of several runs with its own events: hordes, elites, storms, toxic clouds, supply drops, survivor signals. Clear territories for resources, build outposts, take contracts from the radio tower. But victory isn't clearing the map: you have to reach the four invasion points and drive each faction out of its lair. Each one has its own enemies, its own boss and its own ending.

A Story Where You Decide

As the story unfolds, you will have to choose who to take into the convoy, who to make a deal with and who to fight.

Build Your Base

Bring survivors home. Build a garage, a workshop, an arsenal, a hospital, a lab, a radio tower. Named specialists unlock new vehicles and weapons — and some of them have a story of their own: not everyone who answers on the airwaves is on your side. Every run makes the base stronger; every radio tower widens the airwaves you can hear.

Features

  • Survivors-like auto-shooter where the hero is a growing armored convoy
  • Hordes of thousands of enemies
  • A severed tail is lost with everything mounted on it
  • Crew works during the run: gunners, mechanics, scavengers, observers
  • Global map: sectors, outposts, contracts, four invasion points
  • Four factions with their own enemies, bosses and endings
  • A branching story
  • Airwaves: radio signals, documents, the world's story in pieces
  • A base with eight buildings and named specialists
  • Four locomotive types — find your playstyle
  • Full controller support — optimized for Steam Deck

October, 1998. You’re alone on the graveyard shift at a small-town radio station. Then the callers start describing the same man.

Late Night with Ken Hayes is a first-person psychological horror game set inside WBRF 98.3 FM during a violent late-night storm.

You are Ken Hayes, the station’s overnight host. Take calls, operate the broadcast desk, make coffee, answer messages and keep the show running while the rest of Briar Falls sleeps.

At first, it’s an ordinary shift.

Then one caller mentions a pale man standing outside.

Another caller sees him too.

And every time someone talks about him on air, he seems to get closer.

WORK THE NIGHT SHIFT

Explore a detailed late-1990s radio station, answer incoming calls and interact with physical broadcast equipment as the familiar routine of Ken’s shift slowly begins to break down.

LISTEN CAREFULLY

The horror unfolds through callers, radio interference, text messages, environmental changes and things that may—or may not—be waiting just outside the light.

SOMETHING IS SPREADING

People who have never met begin describing the same figure. What connection does the broadcast have to what they are seeing—and what happens when too many people know he exists?

A SHORT, AUTHORED HORROR EXPERIENCE

A tightly paced, story-driven horror game designed to be played in a single sitting, with a grounded late-1990s atmosphere, heavy rain, practical interactions and escalating supernatural horror.

Law Firm Simulator is a serious 3D management simulation about turning a small legal practice into a respected firm.

Design the office. Hire the right people. Take on the right cases. Every decision affects your team, your finances, your clients, and the future of the firm.

Create an office that supports the way you want to work. Paint rooms, place walls and doors, choose finishes, and furnish offices, reception areas, conference rooms, break rooms, storage, and specialist spaces.

Arrange the workplace around your priorities: prestige, comfort, facilities, efficiency, or a balance of all four.

Build your docket carefully and keep every deadline in view. Review incoming opportunities, understand the client behind each brief, assign the right counsel, and decide how much attention each case deserves.

Cases move through a six-stage workflow:

  • Open and investigate

  • Legal analysis

  • Strategy and negotiation

  • Filing and preparation

  • Hearing and execution

  • Client closeout

Balance favorable outcomes against time, workload, staffing capacity, and financial risk. A full docket is only valuable if your firm can deliver.

Recruit across six roles, from legal assistants and paralegals to associates, investigators, and partners. Match skills to assignments, develop specializations, and build teams that can handle increasingly complex work.

Track workload, stress, satisfaction, salaries, productivity, and career development. A successful firm depends on more than individual talent; it depends on putting the right people in the right place at the right time.

Watch cash flow, revenue, expenses, payroll, retainers, and projected runway. Decide when to grow, when to invest, and when to protect the firm from unnecessary risk.

Your reputation opens new opportunities. Unlock practice areas, recruit stronger talent, develop firm-wide initiatives, and choose the operating principles that define your culture.

Your firm is not operating in isolation. Track rival firms, compare market standing, and respond to a legal market shaped by reputation, outcomes, client relationships, and financial performance.

Choose between a full-firm start with an established team or the more demanding path of a solo practitioner. Name your firm and partners, set the pace of the simulation, and decide what kind of practice you want to build.

Core systems include:

  • Design and furnish a complete 3D law office

  • Manage clients, case opportunities, deadlines, and outcomes

  • Progress cases through investigation, analysis, negotiation, preparation, hearing, and closeout

  • Hire, assign, train, and support a multi-role legal team

  • Balance cash flow, payroll, retainers, expenses, and growth

  • Unlock practice areas and firm-wide initiatives

  • Track reputation, experience, market standing, and rivals

  • Choose between Full Firm and Solo Practitioner scenarios

FULL DESCRIPTION

LAYERED LOOP is a minimalist tower defense game.

Towers in the game automatically level up when conditions are met, gaining increased damage or production efficiency. After reaching a certain level, towers can devour adjacent key structures to evolve, unlocking new abilities or massive stat boosts.

You can build towers on top of existing ones like constructing a skyscraper, with the effects of all layers retained. Once a tower stack reaches 5 levels, it grants various global buffs based on its composition.

Build endless towers in limited spaces to fend off the endless waves of enemies!

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

THE CORE

At the center of this circular world lies a living Core.

Enemies surge toward it endlessly.

You have only one mission: build defenses and protect the Core.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

CORE MECHANICS

  • MODULAR STACKING AND MIRACLES (5-LAYER WONDERS)

  • Stacking — After a tower is passed by a hero a certain number of times and reaches a set level, you may build a new structure on top of it, just like on a normal tile.

    The cost: all layers below the top one lose their growth ability.

  • Miracle — Layer 1 → 2 → … → 5.

    When a stack reaches 5 layers, a Miracle awakens, granting powerful global buffs to all structures on the field.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

  • EVOLUTION SYSTEM

Each structure has 3 evolution stages.

Each evolution requires reaching a certain level and consuming an adjacent Key structure, in exchange for far greater power.

  • Tier 1: Primitive Form

  • Tier 2: Enhanced Variant

  • Tier 3: Ultimate Form — beyond the ordinary

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

  • SYNERGY & RESONANCE

  • Synergy — Structures affect one another:

    • Data Station (S): generates Data Energy

    • Defense Tower (D): converts Data Energy into bullets

    • Booster (B): increases fire rate of nearby structures

    • Amplifier (A): exponentially boosts damage of lower layers

      And more.

  • Resonance — When a hero passes by, different structures trigger different effects:

    • Passing S grants Data Energy

    • Passing D refills its Data Energy

    • Passing L gives free draws, etc.

      Resonance is also a required condition for stacking.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

  • HERO JOURNEY

Each hero has unique active and passive abilities, supporting different build strategies.

Heroes with built-in weapons let you skip early towers and focus on economy.

Economic heroes allow you to prioritize defense.

Over 20 heroes in total, each offering a distinct playstyle.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

  • BUILDING TYPES

24 core building families, each with unique personalities:

  • Generators (S-Type): Produce power. Amplify allies. The backbone of your economy.

  • Turrets (D-Type): Eliminate threats. Scale with evolution. Your fist against chaos.

  • Logistics (L-Type): Trade resources. Open portals. Enable endless growth.

  • Amplifiers (A-Type):Enhance everything nearby. The multiplier of power.

20 More Esoteric Types: Each waiting to reveal their secrets...

Every run is unique. Every failure teaches. Every success validates your mastery.

WHY LAYERED LOOP?

This is not a game of reflexes.

This is a game of thought.

This is not a game of randomness.

This is a game of intention.

This is not a game of grinding.

This is a game of elegance.

In a world of visual noise, LAYERED LOOP whispers.

In a world of complexity, LAYERED LOOP reveals the beauty of order.

Stand at the center. Build with purpose. Defend the Core.

Let miracles prove your mastery.

A survivors-like where you draw your weapon — literally.

There are no auto-attacks and nothing to aim. The line you draw just by walking IS the weapon: enemies touching your trail get shredded, and the instant a loop closes, everything inside goes up at once. The more you trap, the bigger the boom. Your route is the build.

🪢 Combat by drawing

  • Trail contact deals damage over time; close a loop for a massive burst

  • Sweep up the whole horde with one giant circle, or execute elites with tiny precise loops

  • Dash out of danger and manage your trail gauge to survive

⚡ 30+ upgrades, awakenings, and hidden synergy pairs

  • Pick 1 of 3 every level; max an upgrade to unlock its awakened form

  • 26 hidden synergy combos ("Execution + Insight = Reaper's Ledger") — fill the codex

  • Road rollers, burst kimbap, red traffic lights… street-commute-flavored arsenal

🧿 Charm deck meta-progression

  • Spend run gold on 18 collectible charms, level them up

  • Set bonuses (Berserker, Gale, Harvest, Immortal, Binding) shape your starting build

  • 5 playable characters with distinct styles, plus per-stage Overtime Conditions you toggle yourself

  • 10 stages, each with its own enemy waves, mid-boss, and boss

15-minute runs. Infinite "just one more".

The wind is real. The sea wants to sink you. The note comes due whether you made port or not.

Leeway is a trading sim of the age of sail, built on a sailing model you have to learn. Every wind shift and every shot is simulated, and the sea does not wait for you to be ready.

THE WIND IS THE MECHANIC

  • Apparent wind. Sail faster and the breeze you feel moves forward and hardens.

  • A no-go zone you tack out of. No rig sails into the eye of the wind, and a square rig cannot point as high as a fore-and-aft one.

  • Trim, reef and heel. Sheet in too hard in a blow and she lies over and stops pulling. Reef down and she drives again.

  • Leeway, which gave the game its name. She does not go where she points. She goes where the water lets her.

  • Cargo is weight. A full hold makes her slow to gather way, lets a rogue sea swamp her sooner, and can shift and put a list on her.

THE NOTE COMES DUE

The boat is not yours. You sign a note for her, and interest runs on what you owe. Fall far enough behind and the harbour takes your cargo to cover it.

  • Nineteen goods across a chain of island ports, three of them contraband.

  • Prices move with supply, with festivals and trade wars, and with how well the harbourmaster knows your face.

  • Commissions, blockades, wrecks and dig sites.

  • Merchants do not win gunfights. Run, dump a decoy, signal the navy, or get behind the headland before she does.

OR FLY THE BLACK FLAG

A second campaign with its own economy, on the same sea.

  • Hunt merchants for what is in the hold. Round shot, chain and grape each cut a different way.

  • Subdue, do not sink: a ship on the bottom pays nothing, so board her.

  • Five black-flag hulls, from the Corsair sloop to the three-masted Leviathan.

  • Heat, bounty, fences and a black market, and a navy that escalates until somebody comes for you by name.

THE SEA

  • Every campaign is a new archipelago, with its own wind, currents, storms and wrecks.

  • Storm cells you see coming from far off, to dodge or drive through.

  • Rain, fog, squalls, and a barometer that reads the weather before you can see it.

  • Three endings, earned three ways: brave the Eye, break your rival, or take the host that holds El Dorado.

SAIL WITH FRIENDS

Share a sea with friends over a private room code, or open it for anyone to join. Play is peer to peer and best effort: merchants in co-op, or the pirate hunting the merchant. There is no dedicated server. The whole game is there for one player, offline, and always will be.

AT A GLANCE

  • Not a survival game: no crafting, no hunger bar, no base building.

  • Four presets from Calm to Maelstrom (Maelstrom opens once you have won on Intense), plus separate raider aggression.

  • Seamanship from Deckhand, where the hands trim and reef for you, to Master, with no autotrim at all.

  • Five save slots, photo mode, Steam achievements, Low, Medium and High graphics presets.

  • Colour-blind modes, high contrast, text scaling, captions and reduced motion.

  • Interface translated into every language Steam lists for this game; a few of the newest sailing lessons are still in English.

Important: Input Device Notice

This game is designed around pressing multiple keys simultaneously.

For the best experience, we recommend using a keyboard that supports NKRO (N-Key Rollover) or has strong multi-key input capabilities.

On some standard keyboards, pressing multiple keys at once may result in input errors or unintended input limitations.

If your inputs are not being recognized properly, please use the in-game ghosting test to check whether your keyboard can register at least 12 simultaneous key presses.

Please also note that certain international keyboard layouts (such as AZERTY, QWERTZ, or other non-standard regional layouts) may not fully support all required key positions used in the game.

Lexip is a cozy fantasy factory-building game about industrial magic, rail logistics, and questionable sustainability. You establish a production colony on a strange planet, mine resources underground, process them through layered production chains, and export goods through portals to demanding clients.

Instead of power grids, you rely on local magic. Magic emitters keep your machines running, but they leave behind Null pollution that spreads, transforms terrain, and gradually changes how you plan your factory. Efficiency matters, but clean production, careful logistics, and a healthy respect for the Mage Guild can be just as important.

Key Features:

  • Build and optimize factories with machines, transport routes, shafts, portals, and utility networks.

  • Plan across multiple world layers: the overworld supports settlement, trade, and visibility, while the underground offers resources and dense industrial space.

  • Replace traditional electricity with local magic that has range, storage, demand, and environmental consequences.

  • Move items, fluids, and gases through separate logistics systems.

  • Research new technologies, unlock buildings, and expand production from simple raw materials to complex magical resources.

  • Complete contracts, buy licenses, and navigate the politely worded bureaucracy of the Mage Guild.

  • Choose whether to expand aggressively, produce more sustainably, or turn the consequences of your factory into later production chains.

  • Use the world editor to create your own maps.

  • Plan, save, and reuse factory layouts with the blueprint editor.

  • Create your own content with a full mod editor for buildings, recipes, resources, research, contracts, localization, and other data-driven game content.

Lexip is being built by a very small one-person indie studio. That is why the game puts a strong focus on systems that can grow: data-driven content, modding, reusable blueprints, and editor tools that let players create their own worlds, factory layouts, and game content.
